correctness.rationale: For composite \(n\), the second-largest divisor is \(n/p\) for the least prime \(p\), and the remaining alternating tail is a nonempty sum of positive paired differences, hence at least \(1\). Writing \(\Delta=R+T\) with \(T=n(1-1/p)-\varphi(n)\) gives exact control. Prime powers have the closed form \(\Delta(p^a)=(p^{a-1}+(-1)^a)/(p+1)\). If at least two distinct primes divide \(n\), the second-smallest prime \(q\) gives \(T\ge n(p-1)/(pq)\ge p-1\), hence \(\Delta\ge p\); equality at gap \(2\) then forces \(n=2q\). The packaged verifier independently confirms every equivalence through \(200000\) and matches the first thirty terms of OEIS A382545.

value.rationale: The gap \(\Delta=\chi-\varphi\) is the exact invariant created by the recently resolved Atanassov inequality and is independently maintained as OEIS A382545. Classifying the equality layer and the first two positive layers is the natural sharp next question after nonnegativity. The answer is structural rather than a table lookup: it separates primes, all prime squares, two isolated prime powers, and the infinite semiprime family \(2q\), and proves that no other factorization type occurs.
